system.name: TetriServe
system.one_liner: a DiT serving system using step-level sequence parallelism and round-based scheduling to maximize SLO attainment

components.name: Request Tracker
components.role: records each request's resolution, state, and deadline, and receives request status updates from workers

components.name: Scheduler
components.role: applies a deadline-aware GPU allocation policy and packs requests into scheduling rounds

components.name: Deadline-Aware GPU Allocation
components.role: determines GPU allocation (step numbers per GPU) for each request for one scheduling round

components.name: Round Request Packing
components.role: jointly packs requests into the current scheduling round to minimize late completions

components.name: Execution Engine
components.role: runs the dispatched requests on GPU workers to compute diffusion steps

components.name: GPU Worker-0
components.role: one of 8 GPU workers executing diffusion steps for assigned requests

components.name: Latent Manager
components.role: manages intermediate latents (e.g., R1, R2) produced by GPU workers during diffusion

components.name: R1
components.role: intermediate latent state for Request 1 tracked by the Latent Manager

components.name: R2
components.role: intermediate latent state for Request 2 tracked by the Latent Manager

flows.what: submitted request steps (GPU allocation per request)

content.key_idea: TetriServe centers on a round-based loop where the Request Tracker feeds deadline information to the Scheduler, which allocates GPUs at the step level and dispatches requests to the Execution Engine, whose workers update shared latents and report completion status back to the tracker.
content.reading_order: Top-left Request Tracker with request table (R1, R2 with step counts), arrow 1 to Scheduler (top area with GPU allocation and packing sub-blocks), arrow 2 to Execution Engine's GPU workers (top-right), arrow 3 into Latent Manager, arrow 4 back down to Request Tracker.

summary: This figure shows TetriServe's overall architecture together with a concrete request lifecycle example. Three main components are drawn: the Request Tracker (top-left), which records each request's resolution, state and deadline in a colored table (Request 1 in orange running 20 steps on 2 GPUs, Request 2 in blue running 15 steps on 1 GPU); the Scheduler (top-middle), containing a deadline-aware GPU allocation policy and a round-based request-packing mechanism; and the Execution Engine (right), with 8 GPU workers computing diffusion steps and a Latent Manager tracking each request's intermediate latents (R1, R2). Four circled numbers trace the lifecycle: (1) the tracker informs the scheduler of incoming requests, (2) the scheduler submits request steps to the execution engine, (3) workers produce latents managed by the latent manager, and (4) workers report status back to the request tracker, closing the loop each round.
summary_zh: 该图展示TetriServe的整体架构与请求生命周期：请求跟踪器记录请求的分辨率、状态和截止时间（如橙色请求1用2个GPU跑20步，蓝色请求2用1个GPU跑15步）；调度器进行截止时间感知的GPU分配与请求打包；执行引擎中的GPU worker计算扩散步骤，由潜变量管理器管理中间结果，四个编号步骤展示了请求从提交到状态回传的完整闭环。
